units.title: 1. MND Classification and Features of ALS
units.guide:
MND is anterior horn cell disease of α/γ motor neurons at the ventral horn. Classification: pure UMN = primary lateral sclerosis; UMN+LMN = ALS (90% sporadic, 10% genetic copper-zinc superoxide dismutase defect); pure LMN = SMA, X-linked Kennedy disease and multifocal motor neuropathy with paraproteinemia.
ALS: age >50, M>F, survival maximum 3 years. LMN degeneration of AHC and medullary nuclei 9-12; UMN degeneration of CST and the printed corticospinal tract (CBT). Cognition, HMF, ANS and sensory system are spared. AHC is the 1st structure to degenerate; CST gives brisk reflexes and loss of dexterity/tone. Presentation is distal asymmetric UL (classically forearm/hand) atrophy with fasciculations and cramps.

units.title: 2. Bulbar versus Pseudobulbar Palsy, Diagnosis and Treatment
units.sec: Bulbar vs Pseudobulbar, Imaging, EMG & Treatment
units.guide:
Bulbar palsy (40% pts) is LMN of cranial nerves 9-12: nasal twang regurgitation, flaccid fasciculating tongue, bulbar dysarthria progressing to dysphagia, absent gag. Pseudobulbar palsy (25%) is UMN fibres to 9-12: dysphonic (laryngeal > nasal) with aspiration risk, brisk jaw jerk and emotional incontinence, small spastic tongue, pseudobulbar dysarthria, exaggerated gag.
Photographs: ALS patient with distal UL & LL atrophy; tongue atrophy in ALS; thenar atrophy; thenar > hypothenar atrophy. Needle EMG: polyphasic fasciculations and fibrillations. MRI: B/L symmetrical high intensities. Treatment: no effective drugs; riluzole and edaravone maybe tried.

units.title: 3. ALS Variants — Kennedy, Hirayama and Madras MND
units.sec: ALS Variants: Kennedy, Hirayama & Madras MND
units.guide:
X-linked SMA (Kennedy's disease) is pure LMN trinucleotide-repeat disease with androgen insensitivity and spinobulbar involvement: tremor + fasciculations, proximal wasting = pseudohypertrophy of calf muscles, tongue wasting + perioral fasciculation.
Benign monomelic amyotrophy (Hirayama's disease): young male (<20 yrs), asymmetrical UL weakness + wasting, non-progressive; MRI impingement of dura from tight dural canal tearing in flexion/growth discrepancy, with atrophy/thinning of C8-T1.
Madras MND: bilfacial weakness + ocular involvement + SNHL + asymmetrical atrophy of limbs; a variant of MND. MRI of BMA and clinical photos A-D are labelled Finding of Madras MND.
